text.insert: The migration uses an archive-first replacement, not an in-place cleanup. The current ledger remains available as historical input. New canonical stores begin empty, receive only records that pass typed classification and evidence gates, and become the inputs to a clean graph and search rebuild.

props.title: Decision — selective canonical migration with deterministic projection wipe

text.insert: Always wipe and rebuild derived graph, FTS, target-card, ranking, and dashboard projections. Do not wipe raw source corpora, run-state attempts, PR archives, Discord archives, or the original ledger snapshot. Populate the new semantic store only from safe imports and fresh curation. If the audit classifier cannot separate semantic content reliably, import no legacy semantic assertions and rebuild expert memory from freshly cited evidence.

text.insert: When to Use a Full Semantic Reset

Choose the full semantic reset when legacy records cannot be classified reproducibly, evidence references cannot be resolved at useful rates, subject anchors cannot be mapped without guessing, or an evaluation sample shows unsafe semantic imports. The reset still preserves the raw ledger and source archives. It starts the new semantic store empty, retains observed attempt history from run state, and rebuilds semantic memory through targeted curation of high-value files and functions.
